That usually happens when the provider returns the actions in a different order than your config declares them. Check whether you have multiple default_action blocks; Terraform compares them as an ordered list, so the API's order wins. Declaring them in the same order the API returns, sorted by their order attribute, normally stops the churn. Some people just add lifecycle { ignore_changes = [default_action] } and move on.
ignore_changes feels like a hack tbh

It is a bit of a blunt tool, since it would also hide real changes to the listener. Setting an explicit order value on each action and matching that order in the config is the cleaner fix. If you're on an old provider version, upgrading also helps; a few versions had a known ordering bug here.

I have 2 regular clients, a cooking channel and a fintech startup. do they need to write letters?

Yes, letters of intent (Absichtserklärungen) from both are very helpful: on their letterhead, signed, saying they plan to keep working with you and roughly how much. Ideally they're dated within the last few weeks. You could also ask a Steuerberater to prepare the income forecast so the numbers look credible.

messages.text: need help writing a firm but polite reply to my ex-landlord. he's keeping RM 1,800 of my deposit for 'repainting' and a sofa stain

Happy to help. A few things make a reply like this much stronger: what your tenancy agreement says about deductions, whether you have photos or an inventory from when you moved in, and whether he's given you receipts or quotes. Do you have any of those?
agreement says tenant pays for damage 'beyond fair wear and tear'. I have check-in photos from March 2025 showing the scuffs were already there

That's a good position. Scuffs that pre-date your tenancy can't be charged to you, and ordinary marks on furniture after two years are usually fair wear and tear. The reply should stay calm, cite the clause, refer to the dated photos, and ask for the full deposit back by a specific date.
ok. also unrelated but is there a quick way to get my new address on everything? moved to Mont Kiara last weekend, still figuring out the post

A rough order that works: your bank and card providers first, then LHDN for tax, your employer's HR, insurance, JPJ if you have a car, and any subscriptions. Pos Malaysia also offers mail redirection for a few months, which catches whatever you forget.
lol JPJ, I don't even have a car anymore. sold it in jan
Then skip JPJ, that's one less form. Banks and LHDN are the ones that matter most for official letters.
back to the landlord. if he doesn't budge, what are my options?

You have a few. You could get a lawyer to send a letter of demand, which often settles things quickly. You can also file a claim yourself under the small claims procedure at the Magistrates' Court, which covers amounts up to RM 5,000 and doesn't require a lawyer. Mediation is a third route if both sides are willing.
I'll give him till the 15th. if nothing by then I'm filing at small claims myself, not paying a lawyer for 1,800

That's a sensible plan. Putting the date in your email makes it clear you're serious without sounding aggressive. Keep copies of the agreement, the photos and every message, since you'll need them for the claim form.
put it in the draft. and sign it Kavya Menon, not just Kavya, he's very formal

Here's the draft:

"Dear Mr Marsh,

Thank you for your email. Under clause 7 of our tenancy agreement, deductions apply only to damage beyond fair wear and tear. The wall marks are visible in the check-in photos I sent you in March 2025, and the sofa shows ordinary use. I therefore ask that the full deposit of RM 3,600 be returned. If it is not returned by 15 March 2027, I will file a claim under the small claims procedure at the Magistrates' Court.

Yours sincerely,
Kavya Menon"

messages.text: playwright test flaky: login test passes locally, fails ~30% in CI with 'element is not visible' on the Continue button

Intermittent visibility failures in CI usually mean the test acts before the element has settled. Common causes: animations, a loading overlay still covering the button, or CI being slower so a hard-coded wait is too short. Are you using locators like getByRole, and what does the CI environment look like?
already using getByRole. CI is headless chromium in docker. the button slides in from the bottom, 300ms

That animation is the likely culprit. During the slide-in the button can be outside the viewport or partly covered, so the click races it. Use await expect(button).toBeVisible() before clicking, and consider setting reducedMotion: 'reduce' in the CI config so the app skips the animation entirely. Also check for overlays with the trace viewer.
reducedMotion + toBeVisible fixed it, 50 runs green 🙌
Nice result. It's worth adding reducedMotion to the shared Playwright config so other tests with animations benefit, and keeping trace: 'on-first-retry' so the next flaky failure comes with evidence.

Both protect a beneficiary if the client fails to perform. A bank guarantee is the bank directly promising to pay if the client defaults, and it's governed by local law or the URDG rules. A standby letter of credit is technically a letter of credit used as a backup, governed by ISP98 or UCP600, and is more common in US-linked deals. In practice: same purpose, different paperwork and rules.

Happy to help. Can you list each commitment with its usual days and hours? Then we can see where the real crunch points are.

That's roughly 45 hours at Shiftly, 4 hours of tutoring and 6 hours of moderation, plus travel. The pressure points are Tuesday and Thursday, when you go straight from a full day into teaching, and Saturday, which leaves you only Sunday to recover.
exactly 😩 aur Sundays ammi ke ghar lunch hota hai, that's non-negotiable
Then let's protect Sunday completely. For weekdays, try time-blocking: one fixed block for admin and messages, one for deep work, and a hard stop at 6 so you have a real break before tutoring.
pomodoro try kiya tha, didn't work for me, floor pe har 10 min mein koi na koi aa jata hai

btw unrelated, chai mein elaichi daalna pet ke liye acha hota hai? meri colleague kehti hai 😂
Cardamom is traditionally used for digestion and is perfectly safe in normal amounts, though the evidence is modest. It won't hurt, and it makes the chai better either way.
lol ok. back to the week. sabse bura Thursday hai, tutoring ke baad Lumen ka training module bhi karna hota hai

perfect. last cheez: main gaari ke liye save kar rahi hoon, December tak 3 lakh ka target hai. budget split kaise karun?

messages.text: got a nasty one. my lint rule no-floating-promise-in-loop crashes on for-await loops. stack trace says cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'body')
That usually means the visitor assumes every loop body is a block. Can you paste the visitor function?
omg of course. single-statement for await. who even writes that
More people than you'd think, especially in generated code. Add a fixture for the braceless form and one for a nested loop so the regression is locked in.
adding tests now. this bug is why the release slipped btw, 2.0 is going out friday the 18th instead of tomorrow
A few extra days for a crash fix is a sensible trade. It might be worth a short pinned note in the repo so people aren't surprised.
how do I get the fixture to parse with for await outside an async function? parser complains
Either set the parser to sourceType 'module' with top-level await enabled, or wrap the fixture body in an async function. Wrapping is the more portable option across parser versions.
wrapping works. ok unrelated, what does 'emeritus maintainer' usually mean? want to word it nicely for someone stepping back

It's an honorary title for someone who has stepped back from active maintenance but is recognised for past work. They usually keep their name in the README and may keep commit rights, but have no review or triage obligations. Something like "Emeritus maintainers: people whose work shaped this project and who've moved on to other things."
nice. also life update nobody asked for: handed in my notice today, last day at Harbourline is 22 January 🥲
Congratulations! That's a big step. You could also take a proper week off between jobs if the dates allow.
ha I wish, the gap's barely a week anyway. last q: should the rule autofix or just warn?
Warn by default. Moving code out of a loop can change behaviour, so an autofix risks silent bugs. Offer a suggestion fix that editors can apply on demand instead.

messages.text: my lantern shader looks fine in the editor but blows out to pure white in builds. URP, Unity 6. ideas?

Most often it's HDR or tonemapping differing between the editor and the build. Check that the URP asset used by the build has HDR enabled, that your post-processing volume is included in the build scene, and that the shader isn't relying on an editor-only keyword. Colour space mismatches (Gamma vs Linear) can also do this.
it was the volume. it wasn't in the build scene 🤦
Classic. Worth adding a quick checklist to your build script so it can't sneak past again.
next thing: steam page copy. Lantern Moth is a cosy puzzle game where you guide a moth through a sleeping city by lighting lanterns. I'm a solo dev so it has to sound small but polished

Draft: "Guide a tiny moth through a sleeping city, one lantern at a time. Lantern Moth is a cosy puzzle game about light, shadow and quiet streets. Handcrafted by a solo developer." Short sentences work well for capsule text.
love it. what's a sane price for a 4-5 hour puzzle game?
Most comparable cosy puzzle games land between $9.99 and $14.99. With 4–5 hours and a polished look, $12.99 with a launch discount is a common choice.
hmm. what if I made it free with a tip jar
It can work for building an audience, but it's harder to reach wishlist-driven visibility on Steam. Many solo developers do a free demo plus a paid full game instead.
yeah that's the plan anyway. demo goes live 18 March, here in Manchester we're doing a little launch stream at the co-working space
Nice. Announce the stream at least a week before, and pin a wishlist link in chat during it.
also any tips for writing devlogs that people actually read
Lead with a GIF, keep each post to one change or idea, and end with a question. Posting at a steady rhythm matters more than length.
